proofUses.reason: Integrated triangle error. General finite-graph, constant-triangle and strong-triangle assumptions are separated in the article.

Count labelled trees and their required closed edges exactly. Ordered pairs of disjoint components have a finite-population factor that dominates the shared closed-edge factor below p=1/(N+1), yielding the variance bound after summing over sizes.

Retain the cancellation between the falling-factorial and closed-edge quadratic terms. Sum uniform tree-count asymptotics across a band of width I^(-1), then apply the variance bound; no stronger restriction on epsilon beyond epsilon tending to zero and N epsilon^3 tending to infinity is used.

The diverging band count gives lower bounds for every fixed rank. Uniform susceptibility gives the matching upper tail and expectation; bounded negative parts then give convergence of the normalized sizes in mean absolute error.
Extract a connected cycle-rank-two subgraph, classify its degree-two suppression into three forms, and sum valid simple-template embeddings over positive path lengths.

Count ordered tuples of distinct tree components exactly; retain finite-population cancellation uniformly at every fixed factorial order. Alternating finite sums give the Poisson probabilities. Remove the upper cutoff only in distribution, using the leading largest-component law.

Count unicyclic graphs by their unique cycle and rooted forests, bound their expected number at the extreme threshold, and exclude more complex components separately. The Poisson exceedance law gives each fixed-rank distribution with the exact exponential rate.

Use at most N-1 fresh bonds at each exploration step. Realize each Bernoulli variable as a positive Poisson count, bound the row mean by c, and add independent Poisson padding. Dwass and the lower Stirling inequality give the Borel tail with exact rate I.

The exact-rate largest-component bound controls all upper deviations. Uniform tree-count expectations on bands down to size 2/I and variance at most mean control all lower deviations, with a separate endpoint argument for zero padding.

Uniform exponential integrability upgrades fixed-rank weak convergence to every polynomial moment and exponential transforms for absolute parameter below one. The negative-log-gamma mean gives the explicit o(I^(-1)) expectation correction.
Extend uniform ordered-tree tuple counts to mixed factorial moments, identify the joint generating function by independent marking, and transfer interval counts to ordered exponential arrival times.
